items.name: Rezaei: Iran will not remove 'a single particle' of enriched nuclear material from the country
items.headline: Rezaei: Iran will not remove 'a single particle' of enriched nuclear material from the country
items.source: CBS News live (citing IRIB), 11 Nov 2026; Gulf News/Bloomberg 12 Nov (Al Mayadeen interview); CappNotes 11 Nov
items.claim: Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said on 11 Nov (IRIB / Al Mayadeen) that Tehran 'will not remove even a single particle of enriched nuclear material from the country', rebuking a reported element of the proposal Qatari mediators carried to the White House on Monday. Washington lists removal as a key condition for negotiations. DTN and CappNotes tie Wednesday's oil rebound to this statement.

items.name: Russia: offer to take Iran's enriched uranium remains on the table; Tehran told Moscow no material will leave
items.headline: Russia: offer to take Iran's enriched uranium remains on the table; Tehran told Moscow no material will leave
items.source: Iran International liveblog, 11 Nov 2026 15:24 GMT
items.claim: Russian foreign ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said 11 Nov that Moscow's offer to take custody of Iran's enriched uranium remains open and that Tehran alone decides the stockpile's fate. Rezaei said Iran had told Moscow that no enriched material would leave the country. Separately, Russian official Maxim Maksimov (TASS) called the US pressure campaign 'misguided and counterproductive'.

items.name: Rezaei: if US attacks Pickaxe Mountain, Iran will hit all US bases including in Europe - 'NO SAFE DISTANCE. NO SAFE HAVEN.'
items.headline: Rezaei: if US attacks Pickaxe Mountain, Iran will hit all US bases including in Europe - 'NO SAFE DISTANCE. NO SAFE HAVEN.'
items.source: ABC News live, 11 Nov 2026 1:32 PM EST (Al Mayadeen via IRIB); Iran International 12 Nov 09:30 UTC
items.claim: Rezaei told Al Mayadeen on 11 Nov that if the US attacks the Pickaxe Mountain site Iran would target all US bases, including in European countries, and that any new US attack would not last more than 4-5 days. On X he wrote 'NO SAFE DISTANCE. NO SAFE HAVEN. NO IMMUNITY.' Deputy armed forces chief Heydari said an expanded target list beyond the Middle East was prepared; IRGC adviser Naghdi said forces were authorized to retaliate without geographic limits under Mojtaba Khamenei's orders.

items.name: Trump at Arlington: 'We won. It's just a question of when we end it' - wants 'total victory', war to end 'soon'
items.headline: Trump at Arlington: 'We won. It's just a question of when we end it' - wants 'total victory', war to end 'soon'
items.source: ABC News live 11 Nov 2026 1:23 PM EST; Iran International liveblog 17:23 GMT
items.claim: At the Veterans Day ceremony on 11 Nov Trump said 'America did not start a war with Iran', that the US had already won militarily, that Iran would need 25 years to rebuild, that he wants 'a total victory, not a 93 percent victory', and that the conflict 'will be [over] soon' with no timeline. He cited 18 US service members killed.

items.name: Rubio to G7 (closed door, Axios): US 'largely staying the course', won't 'do a stupid deal'
items.headline: Rubio to G7 (closed door, Axios): US 'largely staying the course', won't 'do a stupid deal'
items.source: Fox News live (citing Axios), 11 Nov 2026 ~07:00 EST
items.claim: Per three attendees cited by Axios, Rubio told G7 foreign ministers in Paris that the US was 'largely staying the course', would not 'do a stupid deal', and that the third option is to 'continue to do what we do now'. Trump and Rubio reportedly agree Iran wants a deal but is demanding unrealistic terms; Rubio, Ratcliffe, Kushner and Bessent favor continued economic pressure. G7 ministers pledged to maintain pressure if diplomacy fails.

items.name: WSJ: Vance weighing direct talks with Rezaei, possibly in Doha; Iran says it rejected the request
items.headline: WSJ: Vance weighing direct talks with Rezaei, possibly in Doha; Iran says it rejected the request
items.source: Middle East Eye live, 12 Nov 2026 06:25 GMT (WSJ); Iran International 12 Nov 09:30 UTC; Newsquawk 12 Nov 10:35 UTC
items.claim: The Wall Street Journal, citing several US and Middle Eastern officials, reported that VP JD Vance is considering face-to-face talks with Mohsen Rezaei, with Doha a possible venue; no timing given. Rezaei denied it and Mehdi Mohammadi, adviser to speaker Ghalibaf, said Tehran had rejected the request. Newsquawk notes crude eased on the WSJ headline on 12 Nov. (Update vs 11-11 file: Kalin/Tasnim Qatar-talks item.)

items.name: Ghalibaf: Iran may end 'no war, no peace' through deterrence without talks; US has not answered the seven conditions and asked Putin to mediate
items.headline: Ghalibaf: Iran may end 'no war, no peace' through deterrence without talks; US has not answered the seven conditions and asked Putin to mediate
items.source: Iran International liveblog, 11 Nov 2026 16:33 GMT; straits.live 11 Nov (Saba)
items.claim: Parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said 11 Nov that Iran may end the state of neither war nor peace through military deterrence, potentially without negotiations; that Washington had not answered Iran's seven conditions for reopening Hormuz; and that US officials had asked Putin to mediate. On 12 Nov an unnamed Iranian advisor (Al Jazeera breaking, via Newsquawk 10:53 UTC) said there will be no negotiations if the seven conditions are not met.

items.name: Araghchi (IRNA): Hormuz could reopen within two days if demands are met; conflict 'will not be resolved through military means'
items.headline: Araghchi (IRNA): Hormuz could reopen within two days if demands are met; conflict 'will not be resolved through military means'
items.source: Al Jazeera, 11 Nov 2026 (statement Tuesday 10 Nov to IRNA)
items.claim: Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told IRNA on Tuesday 10 Nov that the Strait of Hormuz could reopen within two days if Iran's demands are met, and that 'the conflict with Iran will not be resolved through military means, nor by intensifying sanctions.' Iran has not published the full list of seven conditions; Rezaei and Araghchi say it includes lifting sanctions, ending the US naval blockade and ending fighting on all fronts including Lebanon.

items.name: Pezeshkian at COP31: negotiations possible but Iran won't yield to pressure; Pakistan's Sharif urges restraint
items.headline: Pezeshkian at COP31: negotiations possible but Iran won't yield to pressure; Pakistan's Sharif urges restraint
items.source: Iran International, 12 Nov 2026 09:30 UTC (events of 11 Nov); liveblog 11 Nov 14:46-16:09 GMT
items.claim: President Masoud Pezeshkian, at the COP31 summit in Antalya on 11 Nov, said negotiations were possible but Iran would not yield to pressure; he invoked the late Ali Khamenei's opposition to nuclear weapons and held talks with Iraq's president and Norway's PM. Pakistani PM Shehbaz Sharif called for restraint and said negotiations were the only path to lasting peace.

items.name: Press TV: Iran and Oman reach agreement on maritime traffic through the Strait
items.headline: Press TV: Iran and Oman reach agreement on maritime traffic through the Strait
items.source: Newsquawk, 12 Nov 2026 06:40 UTC, citing Press TV
items.claim: Iran's state Press TV reported on 12 Nov that Iran and Oman have reached an agreement on maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, while restating that seven conditions must be met for talks and a reopening. No terms were given and there is no Omani confirmation in the fetched sources. Comes a day after Reuters sources said Iran attacked navigation systems on Oman's Didamar island.

items.name: Reuters sources: Iran attacked ship navigation systems on Oman's Didamar island in the Strait
items.headline: Reuters sources: Iran attacked ship navigation systems on Oman's Didamar island in the Strait
items.source: Arab News (Reuters), 11 Nov 2026 06:24 GMT+3, updated 21:20
items.claim: Three sources told Reuters that Iran attacked ship navigation systems on the Omani island of Didamar; Iranian state media said the IRGC destroyed 'enemy navigation systems' there (claimed Tuesday 10 Nov). Reuters verified smoke in video and Copernicus thermal activity but no damage assessment. Two shipping sources and a maritime security source said the impact on commercial shipping would likely be limited. CENTCOM and Oman's media ministry did not respond.

items.name: Ambrey: outbound merchant vessel struck by unknown projectile 14nm NW of Ras Al Khaimah, engine-room fire, no injuries
items.headline: Ambrey: outbound merchant vessel struck by unknown projectile 14nm NW of Ras Al Khaimah, engine-room fire, no injuries
items.source: Devdiscourse (Reuters), 12 Nov 2026 15:15 IST; Newsquawk 12 Nov
items.claim: Maritime security firm Ambrey said a merchant vessel heading out of the Strait of Hormuz was struck on the stern by an unknown projectile 14 nautical miles northwest of Ras Al-Khaimah, UAE, on Wednesday 11 Nov, causing an engine-room fire; no injuries or pollution reported. Vessel type and name not given; no UKMTO advisory mentioned in the fetched text.

items.name: Iran's army says a tanker hit a mine early Wednesday after entering a prohibited area; UKMTO reports a tanker incident, unclear if same vessel
items.headline: Iran's army says a tanker hit a mine early Wednesday after entering a prohibited area; UKMTO reports a tanker incident, unclear if same vessel
items.source: Arab News (Reuters) 11 Nov 2026; Fox News live 11 Nov (AP); straits.live 11 Nov
items.claim: Iran's army said on Wednesday 11 Nov that an oil tanker struck a mine and caught fire after entering a prohibited area; UKMTO separately reported a tanker incident in the Strait the same day (straits.live: the second tanker incident in under 24 hours), and Reuters said it was unclear whether it was the same vessel. The IRGC's running claim is now three tankers hit by mines on 'unauthorised routes' on 10-11 Nov; no maritime authority has confirmed the mine attribution. (Update vs 11-11 file: IRGC 'third mine-struck tanker' claim.)

items.name: IRGC Navy: two supertankers carrying >4 million barrels exploded and are burning on the 'southern route'
items.headline: IRGC Navy: two supertankers carrying >4 million barrels exploded and are burning on the 'southern route'
items.source: TASS, 12 Nov 2026 (dateline Tehran); Newsquawk 12 Nov
items.claim: The IRGC Navy public relations office said on 12 Nov that two supertankers carrying more than four million barrels of oil in total 'stopped after a very strong explosion' and caught fire while sailing the unauthorized southern route of the Strait despite warnings from its 'Hormuz Strait traffic control center'; it did not say what caused the explosions and warned any vessel that turns off navigation systems and cooperates with US forces would face the same fate. No vessel names; no UKMTO/Ambrey confirmation in fetched sources. Brent spiked to a 93.94 session high on the headline then unwound (Newsquawk).

items.name: Saudi-led coalition: 3 Houthi cruise missiles toward Riyadh and 2 drones intercepted 11-12 Nov; Houthis claim KKIA hit
items.headline: Saudi-led coalition: 3 Houthi cruise missiles toward Riyadh and 2 drones intercepted 11-12 Nov; Houthis claim KKIA hit
items.source: House of Saud (citing Asharq Al-Awsat, Anadolu, Xinhua, Reuters), 12 Nov 2026 09:44 UTC
items.claim: Coalition spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Maliki said in two statements (evening 11 Nov and early 12 Nov) that three Houthi cruise missiles launched toward the Riyadh region were intercepted and destroyed, and two drones were shot down over Makkah and the southern border. Saudi Civil Defence said debris from two intercepted ballistic missiles fell in the Makkah region. Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree claimed the cruise missiles hit King Khalid International Airport. DTN separately notes Houthi missiles at East-West pipeline pumping stations on Tuesday (already recorded).

items.name: Bessent moves to a military base after Iranian threats reach 'more than an advanced stage'; Miller and Rubio also relocated
items.headline: Bessent moves to a military base after Iranian threats reach 'more than an advanced stage'; Miller and Rubio also relocated
items.source: Fox News live, 11 Nov 2026 (senior administration official)
items.claim: A senior administration official said Iranian threats against Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, described as the architect of 'Operation Economic Outcast', had reached 'more than an advanced stage', so he and his family moved to a military base; a Treasury spokesperson said he 'will not be deterred'. The update adds that Stephen Miller and Rubio have also moved to military or protected housing in recent weeks.

items.name: Baghaei (ISNA): US 'falsely portrays itself as a victim of Iranian terrorism', accuses Washington of war crimes and state terrorism
items.headline: Baghaei (ISNA): US 'falsely portrays itself as a victim of Iranian terrorism', accuses Washington of war crimes and state terrorism
items.source: Newsquawk, 11 Nov 2026 23:30 UTC, citing ISNA
items.claim: Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei said via ISNA late 11 Nov that the US falsely portrays itself as a victim of Iranian terrorism, and accused Washington of war crimes and state terrorism. Rhetorical, no policy content.

items.name: Allianz Trade: physical war damage across Gulf states 'just above $200bn', mostly in Hormuz-locked economies
items.headline: Allianz Trade: physical war damage across Gulf states 'just above $200bn', mostly in Hormuz-locked economies
items.source: CBS News live, 11 Nov 2026
items.claim: Insurer Allianz Trade reported on 11 Nov that physical damage across the Gulf region from the Iran war is assessed 'just above $200bn, mostly concentrated in Hormuz-locked economies', with total economic costs possibly reaching about four times that by 2030.

items.name: Reuters: 'Hormuz traffic is up. So are the attacks' - 37 vessels hit in October, charter rates above $1m/day, 130 IMO-confirmed incidents since 28 Feb
items.headline: Reuters: 'Hormuz traffic is up. So are the attacks' - 37 vessels hit in October, charter rates above $1m/day, 130 IMO-confirmed incidents since 28 Feb
items.source: BOE Report (Reuters), 11 Nov 2026 16:04 UTC
items.claim: Reuters reported 11 Nov that 37 vessels were hit in October (Washington Institute), the worst month of the war; IMO has confirmed 130 incidents and at least 25 seafarers killed since 28 Feb; 11 supertankers damaged by 23 Oct. S&P Global counted 31 LNG tankers leaving the strait in October vs 23 in September, with UAE LNG traffic back to prewar levels and Qatar at just over 30%. Charter rates are above $1 million a day, crew hiring costs tripled; no war-risk premium figure printed.

items.name: OPEC MOMR: October output +2 mb/d to highest since the conflict began; Saudi +26%
items.headline: OPEC MOMR: October output +2 mb/d to highest since the conflict began; Saudi +26%
items.source: DTN, 11 Nov 2026 9:11 AM CST; Gulf News/Bloomberg 12 Nov
items.claim: OPEC's monthly report published Wednesday 11 Nov showed output rose 2 million b/d in October to the highest since the conflict began, led by Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Iraq; Saudi Arabia told OPEC its output rose 26% in October and Iraq hit a wartime high. DTN: Iranian strikes on commercial vessels 'seemed to have done little to disrupt crude supply'; Saudi crude routed via the East-West pipeline to the Red Sea.
